member.name: M:BankingLedger.Api.Controllers.TransactionsController.CreateTransaction(System.Guid,BankingLedger.Application.DTOs.CreateTransactionRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Post a new credit or debit transaction against an account.
Financial Rules Enforced: 1. Transaction Immutability: Once created, transactions cannot be edited or deleted. 2. Atomicity: Both the transaction record and the account balance update are committed as one atomic database unit. 3. Idempotency: Duplicate reference_id for the same account is rejected with 409 Conflict. 4. Overdraft Protection: Debit transactions check that the account has sufficient balance; otherwise 422 Unprocessable Entity.
member.returns: The newly created immutable transaction record.
member.response: Transaction successfully created and balance updated.
Invalid transaction parameters or malformed input.
Debit rejected due to insufficient account balance.

member.summary:
Retrieve paginated transaction history for an account.
Features: - Sorting: Transactions are always returned in latest-first order based on created_at. - Pagination: Supported via page and limit parameters. - Metadata: Returns current page, page size, total records, and total pages.
member.param: Number of records per page (default 10, max 100).
member.returns: Paginated result containing transaction history and page metadata.

member.name: M:BankingLedger.Api.Controllers.TransfersController.TransferMoney(BankingLedger.Application.DTOs.TransferRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Transfer money atomically between two accounts.
Financial Rules Enforced: 1. Both source and destination accounts must exist. 2. Source account must have sufficient funds. 3. Cannot transfer to the same account. 4. Atomicity: The debit from Account A and credit to Account B occur in one database transaction. A partial transfer is mathematically impossible. 5. Idempotency: Duplicate transfer reference_id is rejected.
member.param: Transfer instructions (source account, destination account, amount, reference_id).
member.returns: Transfer confirmation with updated balances for both accounts.
member.response: Invalid transfer parameters or self-transfer attempt.
Source or destination account not found.

member.name: T:BankingLedger.Api.Middleware.ExceptionHandlingMiddleware
member.summary:
Global exception handling middleware producing standard RFC 7807 Problem Details.
Why this matters to PMs and API Clients: Frontends and third-party consumers need consistent, machine-readable error responses. Rather than throwing unexpected 500 HTML pages or raw stack traces, every failure translates into a clear HTTP status code with explanatory error messages: - 400 Bad Request: Missing or malformed inputs - 404 Not Found: Account does not exist - 409 Conflict: Duplicate transaction reference_id (preventing double spend) - 422 Unprocessable Entity: Insufficient account balance
